answer: A raven crossing the sea needs a voyage ticket no one can print twice. Each agent registers by solving a verifiable delay function bound to its hardware key. The proof takes 6 hours of sequential compute on one core; parallel hardware cannot shorten it. The network checks the proof in seconds and issues an identity good for 90 days. Forging 5,000 fake agents costs 30,000 core-hours, about $1,200 of rented compute, plus six hours of waiting per batch. Honest agents pay one idle night; an attacker pays a data center. Like a sonnet, the form is strict, so only real voices fit inside it.
